reading:
What the judges love in Pocket Timeline is the time on one line, and they have loved it in every round. In the main round the costume sank it: pixel faces, an olive ground, berry NOW and cartridges (5.11). Every lens still said to keep the NOW/NEXT/LATER spine. Traced (7.71, #3 in tour round 1, 6 top fours, 6 promise votes, first with system and skeptic) earned its place by drawing time in light wherever there is time: lit NOW and NEXT plates with the lit spine between them, the four-week pulse trace on NEXT's tube ("the best data-in-light figure in the heat"), To do as a due queue cut by a lit NOW line with SOMEDAY below, Plans as an agenda that folds its quiet weeks beside a month tube with pulses, and Chat's axis ending in the box tabbed NOW. Its three faces each have one job: condensed Instrument Sans for display, Plex for reading, Plex Mono for every date. Links are denim and underlined, and no target is small.

What held it back is weight and leftover costume, not the idea:
- A boxed 'Edit, complete, or snooze' button on every To do row. Seven lenses named it.
- Two ways to add on To do.
- Notched cartridges in Lately added and cards on Ideas. Six lenses named them.
- Memory, Family and Status folded into Settings on the phone.
- Status as a three-column grid, with no figure at the top and a spine that means nothing there (the skeptic: "decoration").
- '1 WK/DIV' jargon, and 10px day numbers on the trace.
- Amber leaking out of its one job: a lemon To do spine, an amber '4 shown' node, the restaurant kind in amber, and an amber afterglow on the cards.
- Thick lens cases, a Chat elbow that "looks accidental", and a day stop off the line on the phone.
- A generic column of boxes on Home's right side, and Coming up rows with an empty middle.
- A title that says 'next' three times on one screen.

The refine's lesson: in heat a, refinements that only cleaned up looked like their parents at thumbnail size. They won only where the fixes were new drawings. So the fixes here have to show on the page:
- Status as lamps on the line, with the spend tube as its first stop.
- Settings as stops on the line.
- The shelf as one tray on its own short line.
- Ideas as a one-line table.

The graft's lesson: graft in Pocket's own dialect (square stops, lit plates, pulses and figures), choose features that draw data the page already holds, and avoid the heat's convergence on two-sided chats and NOW lines.

Titles: soul, style and system liked 'What's next for us?' where the NEXT plate sits below it. The majority ranked 'What's the plan?' first: feedback, interaction, type, usability and the skeptic, with the tour's lessons agreeing. They said to drop 'next' above a NEXT screen and named the untried 'What's our plan?' for this lineage.

What would make it win: keep every structure, take the weight out, make the line mean time or state honestly on every page, light only what is live (with the kit's full halos), and put the job word in the title.

briefs.name: Traced, Trimmed
briefs.hypothesis: Traced already has every structure the judges asked the lineage to keep, and it came 3rd with six promise votes. Its faults are specific and fixable, and they are about heaviness and unclear signals: boxed row buttons, two doors, cartridges, folded phone navigation, a Status grid, jargon, amber leaks, thick cases and a generic shelf. Fixing all of them wins points on every lens. It also beats the 'refinements look like their parents' trap, because four of the fixes are new drawings that show at thumbnail size: Status as lamps on the line with the spend tube as its first stop, Settings as stops on the line, the shelf as one tray on its own short line, and Ideas as a one-line table. Together with the kit's light on what is live and a title that lights the job word, that should take it past 8 and past both yardsticks.
briefs.brief:
Start from t1-pocket-graft: its palette file, variants/t1-pocket-graft/sheet.css, its templates and static/icons.svg. Copy status.html, settings.html and idea_form.html from /home/user/FamilyDB/src/familydb/web/templates/ to change their markup. Keep every token: bg #0a0e0c, slate surfaces #12171a to #1b2227, steel line #4b5963, bone heading #dcd8cb, denim accent #9db6d6, lit #86d9a6, brand and screen exactly #6dff9c, glow .95, screenGlow 1.0. Write this rule into the sheet's header comment: the line means time or state. - Where a page has time (Home, To do, Plans, Chat, Status's recent activity), the stops hang at their time. - Where it has state (Status's lights, Settings' parts), each node is that row's lamp. - Where it has neither (Ideas, the form, Family, Memory, Your password), the line drops from the title tile to the first section's node and ends in a 10px steel T buffer. It does not run on to the foot. HOME 1. Title (_ask.html):

- Curly apostrophe. Instrument Sans 600, font-stretch 84%, clamp(2.25rem, 4vw, 2.75rem)/1.05, -0.014em, bone. It is the largest head on Home. - .glow takes E1 (0 0 .45em rgb(109 255 156/.45), 0 0 1.3em rgb(109 255 156/.22)). `.welcome:focus-within .glow` adds a third wide layer, 0 0 2.4em rgb(109 255 156/.12), with transition text-shadow var(--afterglow). 2. NOW stop: - The date beside the NOW plate: Plex Sans 500 15px ink-2 in place of mono (system's warmth note). - The NOW plate brightens while you write: `.welcome:focus-within .stop-label .plate { box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px rgb(109 255 156/.6), 0 0 20px -2px rgb(109 255 156/.75) }`, on in 0.12s, fading over 1.2s. So NOW lights when you are at it. - Keep the Vera name tab, E4's resting halo and E7's bottom-left pool through scanlines (`.welcome .ask::before`). - The three ways to start stay as slate keys, 44px, 8px apart. 3. NEXT: - Thin the lens. `.crt`: 3px bezel at the sides and top, a 22px chin, 10px outer radius, 7px glass radius. Case #2c3135 with an 8% white top-edge highlight (E8). Keep the 80px phosphor spill and the power light (E12). - `.next-up::before` reads "Next four weeks": Plex Mono 500, 12.5px, sentence case, no tracking. - Trace labels (`.pulse-day`, `.wk`, `.month-mark`) go from 10px to 14px VT323 on the glass. Only `.pulse.next .pulse-day` is at --phosphor-bright with E13's three halos; the rest are at --phosphor-dim. - The plate keeps breathing. 4. Coming up: - Rows go from 70px to 56px. The leaf shrinks to 44px (`.chip` width 44px; day 1.25rem; month and weekday 11px) and still sits on the line. - A 1px dotted --line-2 leader (`.agenda .what` as flex, with ::after flex:1) runs from the title to the time whenever a time follows. That closes the empty middle. - entry.location goes on a second line in ink-2 15px after the pin icon. - Keep the head figure '4 more after Next up'. 5. LATER: keep the dashed hollow plate, 'All plans' and the dotted run-on. 6. The shelf (`aside.shelf`): the four boxes become ONE slate tray. - Tray: background #11161a, 1px --line edge, 3px radius, padding 1.25rem 1.25rem 1.25rem 2.5rem. - Its own short line: 1px --steel, 1.25rem in from the tray's left edge, from the first head to the last. Each h2 plugs in at an 8px square node: setup amber filled (it needs a look); To do filled steel, turning amber only while a task is late; wishes hollow; Lately added filled steel. - Sections are divided by 1px --line rules, with no inner boxes. - Setup: a 2px amber rule down its left inside the tray, never an amber fill. Steps are numbered in 1px amber squares; links in ink with amber underlines. - To do: head 'To do', then the figure '4 open · 2 late' in Plex Mono 600 figures and ink-2 words. '2 late' is amber and links to url_for('web.tasks', _anchor='task-list'). 'All 4' in denim. The rows keep the lit NOW line plate. - Kids' wishes: names as denim underlined links, not pink; '0 open' in mono ink-2. - Lately added: one-line rows. Keep class "idea-card" on each , because the harness's motion frames hover the first one. - Row: a 28px steel ring holding the kind glyph in the kind's colour (the only place a kind colour appears), the title in Plex Sans 600 16px (nowrap, ellipsis), the kind word in ink-2 14px, then 'for Maya, Theo' in ink-2 and '#1' in mono dim at the right. - Rows are 48px with hairlines between. No chamfers and no caps. - 'Something to eat: 2 restaurants to try' is the last row, drawn the same way, with an arrow. 7. Afterglow (soul's fix): - Applies to every row that is a way in: .idea-card, .agenda > li, .queue .task, the Settings stops and the Ideas rows. - Pointing at a row lights it in 0.12s: background color-mix(in srgb, var(--steel) 13%, transparent) and box-shadow inset 2px 0 0 var(--lit), 0 0 18px -10px var(--lit). - It fades over 1.2s (--afterglow). Never a kind colour, never amber. TO DO (tasks.html) - Page head: title and lede, with the figure '4 open · 2 late' after the title ('2 late' amber, linking to #task-list). No green button in the head. - One door: replace the fake field in details.add-task's summary with a real form on the line's first node: -
- hidden csrf and once inputs - - the page's one lit primary: (E3) - then a denim link, 'More: who, when, a reminder', to #add-task. - details#add-task stays, closed unless the list is empty, with a quiet secondary summary: 'Add with details'. - Keep the Open / Done / Cancelled / All keys and the search. - The node before '4 shown…' becomes hollow steel, not amber. - Every line on the page is steel. Only the title tile carries the To do lemon. - The row's `details.more.edit > summary` becomes a quiet link: pencil icon plus 'Edit', denim, underlined, 44px tall, no border and no fill. The form still opens across the row. - Late rows keep amber tick frames and amber 'was due …' words. The NOW line stays lit and dashed. - SOMEDAY rows print no 'No date' in the margin; the plate says it. This removes the 7px overflow at 1280. PLANS (plans_month.html) - Agenda rows: the leaf on the line, then the title and time on one line ('Pho Oregon' 600 17px, '17:00' in Plex Mono ink-2), and the place on a second line. - Drop the mono 'Tuesday 29 September' kicker, which repeats the leaf (style). - Keep the TODAY row lit, 'Nothing on today.', the folded quiet weeks, the week ticks, and the month tube with its pulses in the thin case. Its legend reads 'This month, a pulse for each plan'. CHAT (chat.html) - Remove the elbow that runs from the page head across to the axis. The head's line ends under the lede in a T. - The axis starts at the first .day-stop, a steel plate centred on the axis with translateX(-50%) on desktop and phone alike, and ends at the lit NOW tab on the box. - Keep both sides, the times and the ticks. STATUS (status.html) - Head: title and lede, then one figure line: '6 working · 7 off · 1 needs a look'. Count it in Jinja from models + keys + services by row.on. '1 needs a look' is amber and links to #attention. - First stop, as NEXT is on Home: a lit NOW plate on the line, and beside it the spend readout moved up out of 'What it has cost'. That is the crt('readout') in the thin case, 20rem wide, with its words beside it: 'About $0.00 of the $2.00 daily limit today', then 'Change the limit'. - Who answers, Keys and Connected to: - Three heads plugged into the line, each over single-column rows. No three-column grid. - Row grid: minmax(12rem, 16rem) minmax(0, 1fr) auto. The name in Plex Sans 600 16px, the detail in ink-2 15px, the state in words at the right (On, Off, No key, Not set up) in Plex Mono 13px. - Rows are at least 44px, with hairlines between, and max-width 48rem. - Each row's lamp sits ON the line as its node: - on: a 10px lit square, #6dff9c with a white-hot core, halos 0 0 6px and 0 0 16px, and E20's 3.2s breathe; - off: a hollow 1.5px steel square; - part: an amber half square. - Under them, one legend line in sentence case: 'Lit: working · Hollow: off · Half amber: needs a look'. - Then 'What it has cost' (the 30-day tables), 'Models and prices' and 'Waiting' plug in at hollow nodes. - 'Recent activity' goes under a steel 'Earlier' plate. Each row.when hangs in the margin left of the line, day over time, as To do's deadlines do, so the line carries time on this page too. SETTINGS (settings.html) - The nine parts become stops on the line in one column, loop `sections | sort(attribute='look', reverse=true)` so the part that needs a look comes first. - Each stop is a 64px row and a link: - a node on the line: amber half for needs a look, filled steel otherwise; - a 36px steel ring with the part's icon (her screen for Personality); - the name in Plex Sans 600 17px; - how it stands in ink-2 15px, at most 56ch; - the arrow at the right. - Hairlines between rows, and the afterglow. - The Setup sentence closes the list after a T buffer. IDEAS (ideas.html) - The cards become one-line rows under a column-head row: 'Idea', 'For', 'Drive', '#', in Plex Sans 600 13px label ink, sentence case. - Each row: a 28px steel ring with the kind glyph in its colour; the title 600 16px followed by the kind word in ink-2; who it is for; the drive in mono ('27 min S'); '#1' in mono dim, right-aligned. - Rows are 48px links with the afterglow. - The line runs from the title tile to the 'Save a thought' node, the filters and the '12 ideas' node, then ends in a T buffer. - The radar lens is thinned as on Home. THE FORM (idea_form.html): the line runs from the tile to the form's node and ends in a T buffer at its foot. 'Add it' is the one lit primary; Cancel is a secondary. PHONE (below 52rem) - Take Memory, Family and Status out of the Settings menu. Show nav.tools' items in the top bar: the mark tile, the wordmark in Instrument Sans 600 condensed 1.05rem, then Memory, Family, Status and Settings as 48px-tall, 56px-wide keys with the icon over an 11px word, drawn like the tab bar. - Hide .menu-household at every width. - Keep the six tabs along the bottom. - Chat's day stop is centred on the line. LIGHT (phosphor_kit.md) - E1 on 'plan'. - E2: the mark and its cursor. - E3 on only one primary per view: Send, Add, Add an idea, Add it. - E4 on fields and the box. - E6: the top haze. - E7 in the NOW box. - E10: the landed flash on #coming, #task-list and #attention. - E12 to E17 in the thin cases. - E19: her screen. - E20: breathing square lamps on Status. - The NOW, NEXT and TODAY plates stay lit glass. Everything else is matte. - Keep the reduced-motion and more-contrast blocks. COLOUR AND TYPE - Amber means late or needs a look, and nothing else. The restaurant kind shows its colour in its glyph only, and the rings are steel. - One link colour, denim, underlined everywhere. - Keep the parent's written scale, with the question at 44px. No tracked capitals on any control or link. Case legends at 12.5px in sentence case. Tabular figures everywhere. Smallest text 12.5px.
briefs.borrows:
The judges' fixes, most-cited first, with the lenses that asked:
1. 'Edit, complete, or snooze' becomes a quiet 'Edit' link: feedback, style, system, interaction, type, usability, skeptic.
2. The Lately added cartridges become one-line rows with the kind in a ring glyph: soul, style, system, type, usability, skeptic.
3. One door on To do, a real quick-add input posting to add_task: system, interaction, usability, skeptic.
4. Memory, Family and Status back out of Settings on the phone: soul, interaction, usability, and the tour's lessons.
5. Chat: the elbow goes, and the day stop is centred on the line on the phone: feedback, system, style, interaction, type.
6. Status: single-column rows, the spend tube as the first stop, a figure line, and every live lamp breathing: style, system, skeptic, soul.
7. Ideas cards become a one-line table: skeptic and usability here, and pocket-refine's usability and skeptic in tour round 1.
8. '1 WK/DIV' becomes plain words, and the trace's numbers go to label size with only the next one lit: interaction, usability, style, soul.
9. Amber for late only: a steel To do line, a steel '4 shown' node, the restaurant colour in its glyph only, and a phosphor/sage afterglow: feedback, soul, system, skeptic.
10. Lens cases thinned to a 2-3px bezel with small radii: feedback.
11. The boxed shelf goes on a short line of its own: style.
12. Coming up's empty middle filled by a leader and the place: system, skeptic, and pocket-refine's interaction and usability.
13. Plans: the leaf and the kicker no longer both say the date: style.
14. Due dates kept inside the page padding: system.
15. One denim for every link: pocket-refine's skeptic.
16. 'next' out of the title: feedback, interaction, type, usability, skeptic, and the tour's lessons.

One small borrowed feature, answering soul's call to bring the light back where it is live: the coupling of light and focus from L100 (Night Timetable r10-wild-3, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-FamilyDB/62374e35-c7e3-5c25-a94d-0502bde8e9d6/scratchpad/harness/rounds/r10/variants/r10-wild-3/sheet.css line 1368, `.welcome .ask:focus-within::before`). Only the coupling is taken: here the NOW plate lights while the box is being written in.

The light returns follow phosphor_kit.md E1 to E20.
briefs.title: What’s our *plan*? It keeps the household voice the lineage's 'What's next for us?' was liked for ('our' for 'us'). It moves the glow to the family's job, as most judges asked: 'plan' covers a weekend, an outing, an idea to keep, the calendar and a reminder alike. It drops 'next', which was said three times over the NEXT plate and the NEXT UP tube. It reads as the family asking itself at the kitchen table and telling Vera the answer, so it is still an invitation. At 16 characters it holds one line at 36px on a phone. The tour's lessons named it, untried, for Pocket.

briefs.name: Pocket Diary
briefs.hypothesis:
A pocket diary is the timeline a family actually carries: big day figures down the margin, the weekend marked, and a key inside the cover. Four of its conventions come from four gems, each rebuilt in Traced's steel line, square stops, lit plates and pulses:
- The dates become type that reads at a glance. The trace's day numbers and the rows' numerals are now the same figures, so the drawing is keyed to its list without a hover.
- The weekend, the unit the family plans in, is shown in light on the glass and on every date stack.
- The code of square stops is explained once, on every page.
- The rows get an afterglow the harness's motion frames can see, stepped like a handheld's screen.

It takes the lineage's most-cited fixes as well. It stays recognisably Pocket: the line, NOW, NEXT and LATER, and the trace. And it stays in the lineage's own dialect rather than converging on the heats' two-sided chats and NOW lines. That should add type, system, usability and soul points to Traced's 7.71.
briefs.brief:
Start from t1-pocket-graft (palette, sheet.css, templates, icons.svg). Copy status.html and settings.html from /home/user/FamilyDB/src/familydb/web/templates/. Keep every token, glow .95 and screenGlow 1.0. Keep the line, the NOW, NEXT and LATER plates, the four-week trace, To do's due queue with its lit NOW line and SOMEDAY, the Plans agenda with its folded weeks and month tube, and Chat's axis ending in the NOW-tabbed box. TITLE (_ask.html):

. Set it as the parent's question: Instrument Sans 600, font-stretch 84%, clamp(2.25rem, 4vw, 2.75rem), bone, E1 halo on 'plan'. It is the largest head on Home. 1. THE DAY NUMERAL, the one date drawing on every page (L153) - Rewrite the chip() macro in _ui.html: {{ parts.day }}{{ parts.month }}{{ parts.weekday }} - CSS: - .day is a two-column grid, column-gap .45rem, align-items center, with no box, border or fill. - .day-n: IBM Plex Mono 400, 2.25rem/.85, letter-spacing -0.05em, font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums lining-nums, colour --heading. Check the zero at this size ('10', '30'); if its mark nags, use Plex Sans 400 tabular. - .day-m: Plex Mono 500 .78rem in --plans. .day-w: Plex Mono 500 .78rem in --label. - .wkend .day-w: --heading, weight 600. - .is-today .day-n: #6dff9c with E1's two-layer halo, the only lit numeral on a page. - Phone: .day-n at 1.875rem. - Home, Coming up: each row is: its 8px node on the line (hollow; lit only for a plan today) | 4.75rem .day | minmax(0,1fr) title (with the place on a second line) | 4rem time | 6rem 'in 4 days'. Rows are 60px. The numerals read down the column like a diary's margin, and each one is the same figure as its pulse on the NEXT trace above. - Plans agenda (plans_month.html): the same row. Drop the mono kicker, which the numeral makes redundant. - To do (tasks.html): `.due-at` in the margin left of the line becomes the numeral ('27') with 'Sep' over '19:56' stacked beside it. On late rows the stack is amber and the numeral stays bone. SOMEDAY rows print nothing in the margin. - Chat: `.day-stop` becomes the numeral with 'Sep' over 'Sun', on a ground-coloured plate (background var(--bg), no border), centred on the axis with translateX(-50%) on desktop and phone. 2. THE WEEKEND, in light (L132) - NEXT trace (the trace macro in _ui.html): - Work out today's weekday as wd0 = ((civil(y, tm, td) | int) + 3) % 7, with Monday = 0 (1 January 1970 was a Thursday). - For each n from -1 to 27 where (wd0 + n) % 7 == 5, emit before the pulses. - CSS: position it with the existing .dN classes, two days wide (one for .w1), from the baseline to the top of the glass, filled color-mix(in srgb, var(--screen) 7%, transparent), with a 1px top edge at --phosphor-dim 30%, under the graticule and the pulses. - The case legend `.next-up::before` reads 'Next four weeks · weekends shaded' in 12.5px Plex Mono sentence case. This replaces '1 WK/DIV'. - Month tube on Plans: `.month-screen :is(td, th):nth-child(n+6)` stained color-mix(in srgb, var(--screen) 8%, transparent), heads included. Today's lit cell wins over the stain. - Plans agenda: Saturday and Sunday rows get a 6% steel wash across the row, the slate version of the same stain. - Every date stack shows its weekend weekday in bone (above). 3. THE KEY TO THE LINE, in every footer (L146 with L135) - In base.html's footer, before the legal line:

Now, or workingA part of the pageStill to come, or offLaterLate, or needs a look

- Each .k::before is an 8px square drawn exactly as the nodes are: - k-now: #6dff9c with a white-hot core, halos 0 0 5px and 0 0 12px; - k-on: filled #707e88; - k-come: a hollow 1.5px steel square; - k-later: a 1px dashed steel square; - k-late: filled amber (--people). - Words in Plex Sans 500 12.5px ink-2, sentence case, 1.25rem gaps. The key sits on its own footer row, starting at the page line's x, so every page's dotted run-on ends at the key. On the phone it wraps to two lines at 12px. - To make the key hold on every page: - Status's round .light dots become the same squares: on = the k-now square with E20's breathe; off = hollow; part = amber. - Settings' part that needs a look gets an amber square node. - Every node on Home, To do and Plans uses only these five marks. - The page's words still say each state. 4. A STEPPED AFTERGLOW on the family's rows (L108) - Token: --row-fade: 1.2s steps(4, end). - The rows that are ways in (.idea-card, .agenda > li, .queue .task, .ideas rows, Settings cards) rest with transition: background-color var(--row-fade), box-shadow var(--row-fade). - On hover or :focus-within they light at once (transition-duration 0s): background color-mix(in srgb, var(--steel) 14%, transparent); box-shadow inset 2px 0 0 var(--lit), 0 0 18px -10px var(--lit). - So the light drops out a frame at a time, like a handheld's screen, and each of the harness's frames at 120, 380 and 900ms catches a different step. - The machine's own light (buttons, fields, lamps, the tubes) keeps E9's smooth 1.2s fade: two materials, two decays. Reduced motion turns it off. - Keep class "idea-card" on the first Lately added row, because the harness hovers it. 5. THE LINEAGE'S MOST-CITED FIXES, in this design's terms - To do: - Each row's summary is a quiet denim pencil-and-'Edit' link, 44px tall, with no box. - One door: a real one-line
posting title to url_for('edits.add_task'), with csrf and once hidden inputs, a labelled input 'What needs doing…' and the lit primary 'Add'. - A denim 'More: who, when, a reminder' link opens details#add-task. - No green button in the head. The head figure reads '4 open · 2 late'. - The To do line is steel, and the '4 shown' node is hollow steel. - Lately added on Home and the Ideas list: one-line rows. - Row: a 28px steel ring with the kind glyph in its colour, the title 600 16px, the kind word in ink-2, who it is for, the drive in mono, '#n' in mono dim. - Ideas gets a column-head row: 'Idea', 'For', 'Drive', '#'. - No chamfers anywhere. Kind colour appears in glyphs only; the restaurant ring is steel. - Home's shelf: keep four separate slate trays, squared to a 2px radius with a 1px --card-edge. - Setup keeps its amber edge. - Kids' names are denim links. - To do's head shows '4 open · 2 late', with '2 late' in amber linking to To do. - NEXT and the month tube: - Thin cases: a 3px bezel, a 22px chin, 10px outer and 7px glass radii, keeping the 80px spill and the power light. - Trace labels at 14px VT323, with only the next pulse's number bright. - Chat: no elbow from the page head. The axis starts at the first day numeral and ends at the NOW tab. - Status: - Single-column rows (name, detail, state in words, lamp) in its slate panels. - The spend readout moved up to the first place under the head. - A figure line: '6 working · 7 off · 1 needs a look'. - Settings: keep the cards, squared, with the one that needs a look first (`sections | sort(attribute='look', reverse=true)`). - Phone: - Memory, Family and Status come back out of the Settings menu as 48px keys, an icon over an 11px word, in the top bar beside Settings. - The wordmark is set in condensed Instrument Sans 1.05rem. - .menu-household is hidden. LIGHT: the kit's E1 to E4, E6, E7, E10, E12 to E17, E19 and E20 as in the parent. The lit things are: - the NOW plate and the NOW line; - the NEXT plate, breathing; - today's numeral; - the next pulse; - the weekend bands on the glass; - the key's first square. Everything else is matte.

briefs.title: Anything to *plan*? It is a diary's open page: the family checking in with each other and inviting Vera to hear anything at all, from a weekend to an idea to keep for someday to a reminder. Unlike 'What's the plan?' it does not presume the family already has a plan, the risk the judges named. Unlike 'Tell Vera what to plan.' it does not read as Vera doing the planning. The lit word is the job itself, and no NEXT glow on the screen claims it. At 17 characters it is the shortest title the tour has seen and holds one line on any phone. It has not been tried.
